content:
This week, Apple continues to steadily expand its Apple Sports app, further strengthening its football (soccer) coverage and offering tennis fans new ways to follow major tournaments. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds multiple new football leagues and tennis schedules

When the Apple Sports app first launched, the experience was quite limited in terms of both supported regions and sports covered.

Since then, the app has made progress on both fronts — its availability has expanded to over 170 countries and regions, while new sports, leagues and events continue to be added.

For example, earlier this year Apple Sports expanded to 90 new countries and rolled out a slew of features centred around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports received another update, with new additions to its football line-up: the Australian A-League Men's, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League and South African Premier League.

In addition, the app now lets tennis fans "follow live draws… including brackets for Grand Slams and WTA 1000 events," according to Apple, allowing users to "see matchups and results for every round at a glance."

Below are the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

Football coverage continues to expand, with new additions including the Australian A-League Men's, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League and South African Premier League. Tennis fans can now use Apple Sports to follow live draws, including brackets for Grand Slams and WTA 1000 events, making it easy to keep track of matchups and results for every round.

Do you use Apple Sports? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
